transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… what brings me in is these strange moments I’ve been having. Like I’ll be in my own house, or at my office, and it suddenly feels not real somehow. It’s hard to explain.

I prepare taxes, so I’m used to sitting at a desk and focusing on numbers all day, and normally that’s very grounding for me, you know? But lately there are times where it feels like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. Like I’m seeing it happen, but I’m not fully in it. It’s unsettling.
Have you been feeling sad or empty lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it sad exactly. It’s more like things that should feel good just don’t land.

My wife will try to joke with me, or she’ll bring up going fishing like we’d planned — and normally I’d look forward to that, I’ve always liked getting out on the water, checking the gear, all that — but lately it’s like that part of me is just… switched off. I know I’m supposed to enjoy it, but I can’t really feel it.
Are you still able to enjoy things that you normally find pleasurable?

Not really, no. I mean, I still go through the motions. My wife will try to joke with me, or she’ll ask about that fishing trip we were planning, and I know those things should feel good. They used to.

I’ve got all the gear sitting in the garage too—rods, tackle boxes, all organized, probably more organized than they need to be. I used to get kind of excited just checking everything before we went. But now it’s like… that part of me that enjoys it has been switched off. I can recognize that it’s supposed to be pleasant, but I don’t really feel it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About two weeks, I think. It started after that client threatened me in my office.

I keep replaying the timing because it’s tax season, and everything already sort of blurs together—appointments, forms, people getting upset about what they owe—but this was different. Since then, these feelings have just kind of been there.
Have you been feeling hopeless about your future?

I don’t know… “hopeless” feels like a big word. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around thinking there’s no future or anything like that.

It’s more like I haven’t been thinking very far ahead. Which is strange for me, because in my line of work everything is calendars and deadlines — quarterly payments, extensions, people bringing in a shoebox full of receipts and acting surprised when it takes time. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess… no, I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. I just haven’t really been able to picture much past getting through what’s right in front of me.
Have you been having difficulty sleeping since you started feeling this way?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, sleep’s been a little… hard to pin down. During tax season my schedule’s never exactly normal anyway, so it’s tough to say what’s from that and what’s from, you know, everything else.

Some nights I look at the clock more than I should, but I also used to do that when I had a pile of returns waiting on my desk. I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really been keeping track.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

I haven’t really noticed, no. I mean, my belt feels about the same, if that counts.

I don’t weigh myself much unless I’m at the doctor’s office, and this time of year I’m mostly sitting at my desk anyway, eating whatever’s nearby between appointments. So… I couldn’t give you a number. Nothing has jumped out at me.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty about anything lately?

I don’t know… guilty, maybe in the ordinary way people feel guilty? Like if I’m behind on returning a call, or if someone’s waiting on documents and I haven’t gotten to them yet. But “worthless” sounds pretty strong.

I’ve always been the kind of person who thinks if something’s on your desk, you deal with it, you know? My father was like that too—he’d keep every receipt in an envelope, which is funny because half my clients still don’t do that.

Sorry, I’m drifting. I guess I haven’t really been thinking of myself as worthless. Guilt… nothing specific comes to mind beyond the usual things.
Have you been experiencing a lack of interest in activities most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not so much that I sit there thinking, “I don’t like anything anymore,” but my wife will try to joke with me, or she’ll bring up going fishing like we’d planned, and I know that should make me feel good.

I used to really look forward to getting out on the water—my dad took me when I was a kid, and I still have this old tackle box in the garage with a busted latch I keep meaning to fix—but lately it’s like… the part of me that would enjoy it just isn’t really coming on. Like it’s switched off or something.
Do you feel that these feelings of disconnection and lack of enjoyment are interfering with your daily life and relationships?

Yeah… yes, it is. I wish I could say it was just me being in a funk, but it’s gotten into work.

I’ve missed several client deadlines, which is not like me. I mean, in tax work deadlines are the whole thing—my old boss used to say the calendar is basically your second spine, which sounds silly, but it sticks with you. And I’ve stopped really seeing people at the office. I keep avoiding clients or coworkers because I don’t trust myself to handle returns right now, or to keep the workplace… safe, I guess. Like I don’t feel reliable in there.

And with my wife, yeah, I think she notices I’m not really there the way I should be.
Have you been feeling that these feelings of disconnection and lack of enjoyment are getting worse over the past two weeks?

It’s been… about two weeks, I’d say. Since that client threatened me in my office.

I don’t know if “getting worse” is exactly the word, but it’s been there since then, and it hasn’t really let up. I keep thinking about how my office used to feel like just… paperwork and coffee and calculators, you know? Not somewhere you’d have to think about that kind of thing.

Sorry—yes, about two weeks. Since that happened.
Have you been feeling that these feelings are significantly impacting your ability to function at work or at home?

Yeah… it really is. Work especially. I’ve missed several client deadlines, and that’s not me—I’m usually pretty on top of that stuff.

And I’ve kind of stopped seeing people at the office. Clients, coworkers… I just avoid them. I keep thinking I’m not in the right state to handle returns properly, or even to keep the place feeling safe right now. It sounds strange when I say it out loud.

At home, I’m there physically, but I know it’s affecting things. My wife can tell I’m not functioning like I normally do.
Have you been feeling that these feelings of disconnection and lack of enjoyment are making it hard for you to take care of your basic needs?

I mean… basic needs, like eating and showering and that kind of thing? I’m doing those, mostly. It’s more that I can’t keep up with the parts of life I’m supposed to handle.

Like at work, I’ve missed several client deadlines, and that’s not like me at all. I’ve stopped seeing people at the office—clients, coworkers—because I don’t trust myself right now to handle returns properly, or to keep the workplace safe. Which sounds odd, I know.

So… not basic needs exactly, but it is making it hard to function.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started feeling this way?

I don’t think so. I mean, my pants don’t feel different or anything like that.

I haven’t been weighing myself, though. We’ve got a scale somewhere, but it’s one of those things that got shoved behind the laundry basket, I think. My wife used to keep track of that more than I did when we were trying to eat better last year—anyway, no, I haven’t noticed any significant weight loss.
Have you been having thoughts of death or suicide since you started feeling this way?

I… I don’t know. Not in a way I’ve sat down and thought through, if that makes sense.

I mean, I’ll have these moments where everything feels heavy, and then my mind kind of jumps around—like I’ll think about what would happen if I didn’t have to deal with all of it, but then I’m thinking about some bill I forgot to mail, or how the garage door’s been sticking again. It’s hard to separate what’s just being overwhelmed from… what you’re asking.

So I guess I’m not sure how to answer that cleanly.
Have you been feeling that these feelings of disconnection and lack of enjoyment are making it difficult for you to make decisions?

Yeah… decisions have gotten weirdly hard.

I’ll sit down with a tax return that I normally could do almost automatically, and I just… stall. I’ll read the same W-2 two or three times, then go back like I didn’t trust what I saw. And then I can’t decide stupid simple things—well, not stupid, but simple—like should I call the client about this now, or should I put the file aside and come back to it.

And then somehow I’m thinking about the old filing cabinets we used to have at my first job, the metal ones that stuck if you pulled the drawer wrong… sorry. Yes. The short answer is yes, it’s making decisions harder.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience any pleasure at all?

I wouldn’t say unable to feel anything good at all, but… yeah, it feels close sometimes.

Like my wife tries to joke with me, and I know I’d normally laugh, or at least give her something back. Or she’ll mention going fishing, because we had talked about that before, and I know that should sound nice. I used to look forward to getting the tackle box sorted—there’s this one lure I always keep even though it barely works anymore—and now it’s just… nothing really lands.

It’s like the part of me that’s supposed to enjoy those things got switched off.
Do you feel like these feelings of disconnection and lack of enjoyment are getting better, staying the same, or getting worse over time?

I think… mostly staying the same. Maybe some days feel a little worse, but it’s hard to tell.

It’s been about two weeks now, since that client threatened me in my office. And I keep thinking, two weeks isn’t that long, right? I mean, tax season days can blur together anyway—sometimes I can’t even remember if I ate lunch or just drank coffee and called it lunch—but since that happened, this disconnected feeling and not enjoying things… it hasn’t really lifted. It’s just kind of been sitting there.
Do you feel like these feelings are significantly interfering with your ability to care for yourself or engage in daily activities?

Yeah… it is. More than I want to admit.

I’ve missed several client deadlines already, which is not like me. I keep looking at returns and thinking, if I make one wrong call here, it’s somebody’s money, somebody’s penalty notice, and then I freeze up. And then I start thinking about the office door, whether someone could just walk in again, and I lose the thread completely.

I’ve also stopped really seeing people at the office. Clients, mostly. I’ve been avoiding appointments because I don’t trust myself to handle the returns properly, and honestly I don’t trust that I can keep the workplace safe right now. Not in a dramatic way, just… I don’t feel steady enough to be responsible for all of it.

So yeah, daily work things are definitely getting affected.
Have you been experiencing any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning as a result of these feelings?

Yeah, I mean… occupationally, definitely. Socially too, I guess, because most of my social contact is through work these days, which sounds sad when I say it out loud.

I’ve missed several client deadlines, and that’s not normal for me. I keep sitting down with the returns and then I just… I don’t trust myself to handle them right. And I’ve stopped seeing people at the office, or I’ve been putting them off, because I don’t feel like I can manage the work or keep the workplace safe right now.

It’s strange, because I’ve had difficult clients before—anyone who does taxes has stories—but this is different. I’m not functioning the way I usually do.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive symptoms to differentiate between mild and moderate depressive episodes
doctor.question: Have you been experiencing any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning as a result of these feelings?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've missed several client deadlines and stopped seeing people at the office because I don't trust myself to handle returns or keep the workplace safe right now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are causing significant impairment in social or occupational functioning.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean… occupationally, definitely. Socially too, I guess, because most of my social contact is through work these days, which sounds sad when I say it out loud.

I’ve missed several client deadlines, and that’s not normal for me. I keep sitting down with the returns and then I just… I don’t trust myself to handle them right. And I’ve stopped seeing people at the office, or I’ve been putting them off, because I don’t feel like I can manage the work or keep the workplace safe right now.

It’s strange, because I’ve had difficult clients before—anyone who does taxes has stories—but this is different. I’m not functioning the way I usually do.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning have been present for approximately two weeks, which meets the duration criteria for a major depressive episode. The patient's symptoms do not appear to meet the full criteria for a more severe or psychotic depressive episode.
